# Chimera AEC — agent catalog

23 specialist agents, 116 engineering skills. Each agent runs inside the multi-agent workflow, is available through `POST /api/v1/analyze` and is callable from the Claude Skill.

| Agent | Discipline | Plan | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Intake & Brief](#intake) | Management | Starter+ | Turns a site and a client brief into an engineering-ready design basis. |
| [Code Intelligence](#codes) | Compliance | Starter+ | Finds the applicable codes, the right editions, and checks every clause. |
| [Architecture](#architecture) | Architecture | Starter+ | Plans the core and negotiates space with structure, fire and MEP. |
| [Geotechnical](#geotech) | Geotechnical | Professional+ | Reads borehole logs and turns them into design parameters. |
| [Structural](#structural) | Structural | Professional+ | Selects the lateral system and designs the frame with a finite-element solver. |
| [Seismic](#seismic) | Structural | Professional+ | Earthquake demand, dynamics and performance assessment. |
| [Wind Engineering](#wind) | Structural | Professional+ | Wind loads, sway, occupant comfort and façade pressures. |
| [Foundation Optimiser](#foundation) | Geotechnical | Professional+ | Compares five foundation systems on capacity, settlement, cost, carbon and time. |
| [HVAC](#hvac) | Mechanical | Professional+ | Loads, ventilation, plant, ducts and thermal comfort. |
| [Electrical](#electrical) | Electrical | Professional+ | Load schedules, transformers, cables, protection, renewables and backup power. |
| [Hydraulic](#hydraulic) | Hydraulics | Professional+ | Water, drainage, pumps, hot water, rainwater and greywater. |
| [Fire Engineering](#fire) | Fire | Professional+ | Egress, construction type, sprinklers and evacuation modelling. |
| [Façade Engineering](#facade) | Façade | Professional+ | Mullions, glass, anchors, thermal bridges, condensation and façade fire risk. |
| [Building Physics & Energy](#physics) | Sustainability | Professional+ | Daylight, glare, acoustics, comfort and annual energy. |
| [Carbon & Resilience](#sustainability) | Sustainability | Professional+ | Embodied carbon by element and system, plus climate-risk screening. |
| [Accessibility](#accessibility) | Architecture | Starter+ | Routes, lifts, gradients and accessible facilities. |
| [Civil & Stormwater](#civil) | Civil | Professional+ | Roof and site drainage, detention and rainwater reuse. |
| [BIM Coordination](#bim) | BIM | Professional+ | Authors an openBIM IFC4 model and finds physical and semantic clashes. |

| [Value Engineering](#ve) | Commercial | Professional+ | Proposes cheaper or lower-carbon alternatives and proves they still work. |

## Intake & Brief <a id="intake"></a>

**ID:** `intake` · **Discipline:** Management · **Plan:** Starter+

Normalises site geometry, occupancy, climate, hazards, budget and performance targets; derives GFA, NLA, height, occupant load, risk category and importance factor; generates a parametric starting scheme.

**Business value:** Feasibility in minutes instead of weeks; consistent design basis for every discipline.

**Skills & methods**
- Occupancy classification (IBC Ch. 3)
- Risk category & importance factor (ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-1)
- Occupant-load estimation
- Parametric grid / core / floor-height generation
- City presets for climate & hazard data

**Inputs**
- Site width & depth
- Building type & storeys
- City / jurisdiction
- Hazard data (wind, Ss/S1, snow, rain, flood, wildfire)
- Budget, EUI & carbon targets
- Priorities (cost, carbon, area, daylight, speed)

**Outputs**
- Design basis
- Derived areas & occupancy
- Initial parametric scheme

**Standards:** IBC 2024 Ch. 3; ASCE 7-22 Ch. 1

**Collaborates with:** All agents (Normalised brief and derived quantities)

**Who buys it:** Developers, Architects (feasibility), Owner's representatives

**Scope & limits:** Hazard presets are regional averages; site-specific hazard data should replace them.

## Code Intelligence <a id="codes"></a>

**ID:** `codes` · **Discipline:** Compliance · **Plan:** Starter+

Resolves applicable standards by jurisdiction, classification and system, controls code editions (current / superseded / pending, project pins) and aggregates clause-level findings with requirement, clause, evidence, value/limit and PASS/FAIL.

**Business value:** Fewer RFIs and permit comments; an auditable trail from requirement to evidence.

**Skills & methods**
- Jurisdiction → standards resolution (US, UK, AU, NZ, CA, SG)
- Edition/version control with project pinning
- Clause-level finding aggregation
- Proxy-method labelling where a local clause is not encoded
- CSV compliance report export

**Inputs**
- Jurisdiction
- Occupancy & height
- Structural material/system
- Standards library

**Outputs**
- Applicable code list with editions
- ~60 clause-level findings
- Version-control warnings

**Standards:** IBC, ASCE 7, ACI 318, AISC 360/341, NDS, NFPA 13/14/72/285, ASHRAE 90.1/62.1/55, NEC, IPC, ADA; Eurocodes & Approved Documents (UK); NCC & AS/NZS (AU/NZ); NBC / CSA (CA)

**Collaborates with:** All agents (Applicable editions and edition warnings)

**Who buys it:** Engineering consultancies, Plan-review / permitting authorities, Code consultants

**Scope & limits:** Decision support; confirm against the licensed adopted edition and local amendments.

## Architecture <a id="architecture"></a>

**ID:** `architecture` · **Discipline:** Architecture · **Plan:** Starter+

Sizes the core for stairs, lifts and risers; receives constraints from fire (exits), structure (wall thickness) and MEP (riser and plant areas); reports net-area impact of every design change.

**Business value:** Protects saleable area by surfacing the cost of every engineering decision immediately.

**Skills & methods**
- Core area planning
- Net lettable area & efficiency
- Lift count estimation
- Impact reporting on design changes

**Inputs**
- Brief
- Fire egress requirements
- MEP riser/plant areas

**Outputs**
- Core dimensions
- NLA / efficiency
- Design-change log

**Standards:** IBC Ch. 10 (via Fire agent)

**Collaborates with:** Structural (Core geometry); Cost & BOQ (Area schedule)

**Who buys it:** Architects, Developers

**Scope & limits:** Rectilinear plates and central cores only.

## Geotechnical <a id="geotech"></a>

**ID:** `geotech` · **Discipline:** Geotechnical · **Plan:** Professional+

Interprets borehole/CPT logs into a soil profile; estimates shear-wave velocity and Vs30 → site class; computes bearing capacity, raft settlement (two stress-distribution methods) and liquefaction triggering.

**Business value:** Early ground-risk visibility before committing to a foundation strategy.

**Skills & methods**
- Imai (1977) Vs–SPT correlation, Vs30
- ASCE 7-22 Table 20.2-1 site class (incl. BC/CD/DE)
- Vesić/Meyerhof bearing capacity
- 2:1 and Boussinesq (Newmark) settlement with 1-D consolidation
- Youd et al. (2001) liquefaction triggering with fines correction

**Inputs**
- Borehole logs (layers, SPT N, γ, cu, φ, Es, Cc, e0, fines)
- Groundwater level
- Founding depth

**Outputs**
- Site class & Vs30
- qult / qall
- Settlement
- Liquefaction FS by depth

**Standards:** ASCE 7-22 Ch. 20 & §11.8; EN 1997-1; IBC §1803/1806

**Collaborates with:** Seismic (Site class → Fa/Fv, SDS/SD1); Structural (Allowable bearing, GWL, liquefaction)

**Who buys it:** Geotechnical consultancies, Contractors (tender), Developers (due diligence)

**Scope & limits:** Correlation-based screening; confirm with site investigation and lab testing.

## Structural <a id="structural"></a>

**ID:** `structural` · **Discipline:** Structural · **Plan:** Professional+

Compares eight lateral systems with FE analysis and ranks them on cost, carbon, area and code path; builds the planar FE model; runs gravity and lateral load cases; checks columns, punching shear and slab depth; iterates member sizes with the seismic agent until drift and strength converge.

**Business value:** Scheme-design structure in minutes with a defensible system choice.

**Skills & methods**
- 2D direct-stiffness frame solver (banded LDLᵀ)
- Automatic system selection (ASCE 7-22 Table 12.2-1)
- Gravity design: ACI 318-19 §22.4.2 columns, §22.6.5.2 punching, Table 8.3.1.1 slabs
- Design-iteration loop (core thickening, outriggers, column/f'c upgrades)
- Structural quantities (concrete, rebar, steel, timber, formwork)

**Inputs**
- Parametric scheme
- Loads
- Site class & seismic parameters

**Outputs**
- Selected system
- Member sizes
- Story forces & drifts
- Utilisations
- Quantities

**Standards:** ASCE 7-22; ACI 318-19; AISC 360-22; NDS 2024

**Collaborates with:** Architecture (Core/column size changes); Cost & BOQ (Quantities); BIM Coordination (Member geometry)

**Who buys it:** Structural engineers, Design-build contractors, Developers

**Scope & limits:** Planar equivalent frame with rigid diaphragm; final design needs a 3D model.

## Seismic <a id="seismic"></a>

**ID:** `seismic` · **Discipline:** Structural · **Plan:** Professional+

Builds the design spectrum, solves modes, runs ELF and CQC response-spectrum analysis with scaling, checks drift, P-Δ and torsion, then estimates performance with a capacity-spectrum pushover and response-history analysis.

**Business value:** Performance-based insight at scheme stage instead of after detailed design.

**Skills & methods**
- Site coefficients & design spectrum (ASCE 7-22 §11.4)
- Jacobi eigen-analysis, mass participation
- ELF (§12.8) and CQC RSA with §12.9.1.4 scaling
- Drift (Table 12.12-1), P-Δ (§12.8.7), torsion (Table 12.3-1)
- Capacity-spectrum pushover (FEMA 440)
- Newmark MDOF time-history with spectrum-scaled record + nonlinear ESDOF

**Inputs**
- Ss, S1, site class, risk category
- Stiffness & mass from the FE model

**Outputs**
- Periods & mode shapes
- Base shear
- Drift/P-Δ/torsion checks
- Performance level
- Ductility demand

**Standards:** ASCE 7-22 Ch. 11–12, 16; EN 1998-1; NZS 1170.5; AS 1170.4

**Collaborates with:** Structural (Drift failures → stiffening requests)

**Who buys it:** Structural engineers in seismic regions, Insurers & lenders (risk), Hospitals & essential facilities

**Scope & limits:** Pushover/time-history are simplified (bilinear ESDOF); not a fibre-section NLTHA.

## Wind Engineering <a id="wind"></a>

**ID:** `wind` · **Discipline:** Structural · **Plan:** Professional+

Computes velocity pressures, the flexible-building gust-effect factor, story forces, serviceability drift, 10-year accelerations, vortex-shedding risk, C&C façade pressures and a pedestrian-comfort screen.

**Business value:** Tells you early whether a wind-tunnel test and damping will be needed.

**Skills & methods**
- ASCE 7-22 Eq. 26.10-1 velocity pressure
- §26.11.5 gust-effect factor (resonant response)
- Along-wind acceleration (C26.11)
- Vortex-shedding screening (EN 1991-1-4 Annex E)
- C&C zone pressures
- Lawson pedestrian comfort

**Inputs**
- Basic wind speed, exposure
- Geometry
- Fundamental frequency & damping

**Outputs**
- Story forces
- Roof drift
- Peak acceleration
- Façade pressure map
- Comfort categories

**Standards:** ASCE 7-22 Ch. 26–27, 30; EN 1991-1-4; AS/NZS 1170.2; ISO 10137

**Collaborates with:** Structural (Wind story forces); Façade Engineering (Design pressures)

**Who buys it:** Tall-building developers, Façade consultants, Structural engineers

**Scope & limits:** Screening only; does not replace CFD or wind-tunnel testing.

## Foundation Optimiser <a id="foundation"></a>

**ID:** `foundation` · **Discipline:** Geotechnical · **Plan:** Professional+

Designs pads, raft, bored piles, barrettes and piled raft for the real column loads; designs piles with α/β shaft friction ignoring liquefiable layers; ranks the options.

**Business value:** Foundations are often 5–15 % of cost; picking the right system early de-risks the budget.

**Skills & methods**
- Pad and raft sizing
- Pile design (α-method clay, β-method sand, end bearing)
- Piled-raft load sharing
- Multi-criteria ranking (cost, carbon, duration, settlement)

**Inputs**
- Column and total service loads
- Geotechnical profile

**Outputs**
- Option comparison
- Selected foundation
- Pile count & length

**Standards:** IBC §1808–1810; EN 1997-1; AS 2159

**Collaborates with:** Cost & BOQ (Foundation cost & carbon); Construction Planning (Duration & rig needs)

**Who buys it:** Contractors, Developers, Geotechnical engineers

**Scope & limits:** Group effects and negative skin friction simplified.

## HVAC <a id="hvac"></a>

**ID:** `hvac` · **Discipline:** Mechanical · **Plan:** Professional+

Zoned cooling/heating loads, ASHRAE 62.1 outdoor air, N+1 chiller/boiler/heat-pump plant, AHU and duct sizing, plant and riser areas and ISO 7730 PMV/PPD comfort.

**Business value:** Right-sized plant and space allocation before architecture is frozen.

**Skills & methods**
- Component cooling/heating loads by zone
- ASHRAE 62.1 Vbz = Rp·Pz + Ra·Az
- Plant selection with N+1 redundancy
- Duct main and riser sizing
- ISO 7730 PMV/PPD

**Inputs**
- Envelope & internal gains
- Climate design data
- Occupancy

**Outputs**
- Peak loads
- Plant schedule
- Duct sizes
- Comfort indices

**Standards:** ASHRAE 62.1-2022; ASHRAE 55-2023; ASHRAE 90.1-2022

**Collaborates with:** Electrical (Mechanical electrical loads); Architecture (Plant & riser areas); BIM Coordination (Duct geometry)

**Who buys it:** MEP consultancies, Mechanical contractors, Facility owners

**Scope & limits:** Peak-load method, not hourly simulation.

## Electrical <a id="electrical"></a>

**ID:** `electrical` · **Discipline:** Electrical · **Plan:** Professional+

Builds the load schedule with demand factors; sizes transformers, the main switchboard and sub-mains (ampacity, grouping and voltage drop); computes fault level; sizes PV, battery storage, EV charging and the standby generator.

**Business value:** Utility applications and electrification plans grounded in real load numbers.

**Skills & methods**
- Demand-factor load schedule
- Transformer & switchboard sizing
- Cable sizing by ampacity and voltage drop (≤ 3 %)
- Prospective fault current
- PV yield, BESS and EV load management
- Generator sizing for life-safety & standby

**Inputs**
- Building loads
- Mechanical loads
- Parking spaces

**Outputs**
- Load schedule
- Single-line ratings
- Cable schedule
- Renewables & backup sizing

**Standards:** NEC 2023 (Art. 210, 215, 220, 450, 625, 690, 700, 706); BS 7671; AS/NZS 3000

**Collaborates with:** Cost & BOQ (Electrical quantities); Carbon & Resilience (PV generation)

**Who buys it:** Electrical engineers, EV-charging operators, Owners pursuing electrification

**Scope & limits:** Simplified diversity; not an arc-flash or coordination study.

## Fire Engineering <a id="fire"></a>

**ID:** `fire` · **Discipline:** Fire · **Plan:** Professional+

Occupant load, exit count, stair capacity, travel distance, construction type & fire-resistance ratings, sprinklers, standpipes, fire-service lifts and smoke control; SFPE hydraulic evacuation model with phased strategy for high-rise and smoke-filling ASET.

**Business value:** Life-safety layout locked in early, avoiding costly core redesign.

**Skills & methods**
- IBC §1004–1017 egress checks
- Construction type & height (Tables 504.3/601)
- NFPA 13 hazard & density
- SFPE hydraulic evacuation model
- Smoke-layer filling ASET vs RSET
- Auto-resolution: adds/widens stairs

**Inputs**
- Occupancy & floor plate
- Core layout
- Height & material

**Outputs**
- Egress design
- FRR schedule
- Evacuation curve
- ASET/RSET

**Standards:** IBC 2024; NFPA 13/14/72; Approved Document B; NCC Vol One Part D/E

**Collaborates with:** Architecture (Stairs & core requirements)

**Who buys it:** Fire engineers, Architects, Authorities having jurisdiction

**Scope & limits:** Simplified smoke model; performance designs need CFD (e.g. FDS).

## Façade Engineering <a id="facade"></a>

**ID:** `facade` · **Discipline:** Façade · **Plan:** Professional+

Sizes mullions and glass for C&C pressures, computes anchor loads, ψ-value thermal bridging, condensation (fRsi), water-test pressure and flags combustible façades.

**Business value:** Façade cost and risk understood at concept stage.

**Skills & methods**
- Mullion deflection & stress (L/175 ≤ 19 mm)
- Glass plate stress
- Effective U with ψ-values
- fRsi condensation check
- Façade fire screening (NFPA 285 / UK Reg 7(2))

**Inputs**
- Wind pressures
- Façade type, WWR, U-values

**Outputs**
- Mullion & glass selection
- Thermal performance
- Fire risk

**Standards:** AAMA TIR-A11 / 501.1; BS EN ISO 13788; IBC §1402.5

**Collaborates with:** Building Physics & Energy (Effective U-values); Cost & BOQ (Façade areas & panels)

**Who buys it:** Façade consultants, Curtain-wall fabricators, Developers

**Scope & limits:** No 2D/3D thermal modelling of details.

Average daylight factor, glare risk, natural-ventilation feasibility, façade sound insulation, overheating; annual and monthly energy by end use, PV offset and scenario comparison.

**Outputs**

**Collaborates with:** Carbon & Resilience (Operational carbon)

**Who buys it:** Sustainability consultants, ESG-driven owners, Certification teams (LEED/BREEAM/Green Star)

## Carbon & Resilience <a id="sustainability"></a>

**ID:** `sustainability` · **Discipline:** Sustainability · **Plan:** Professional+

A1–A5 embodied carbon from quantities, carbon by structural system, lower-carbon options; hazard register (heat, flood, storm, wildfire, earthquake, grid outage) and redundancy assessment.

**Business value:** Embodied-carbon reporting and climate-risk disclosure from the design model.

**Skills & methods**
- Quantity-based LCA (A1–A5)
- System-level carbon comparison
- Future-climate cooling margin
- Hazard exposure × vulnerability scoring
- Redundancy review

**Inputs**
- Quantities
- Hazards
- Plant configuration

**Outputs**
- kgCO₂e/m²
- Carbon hotspots
- Resilience score & mitigations

**Standards:** EN 15978 modules; LETI / SE 2050 benchmarks

**Collaborates with:** Value Engineering (Carbon targets for alternatives)

**Who buys it:** ESG teams, Lenders & green-bond issuers, Developers with net-zero commitments

**Scope & limits:** Generic carbon factors; replace with product EPDs for certification.

## Accessibility <a id="accessibility"></a>

**ID:** `accessibility` · **Discipline:** Architecture · **Plan:** Starter+

**Collaborates with:** Code Intelligence (Accessibility findings)

**Who buys it:** Architects, Public-sector owners, Access consultants

## BIM Coordination <a id="bim"></a>

**ID:** `bim` · **Discipline:** BIM · **Plan:** Professional+

Generates architecture, structure, MEP and fire elements from sized engineering outputs; detects hard clashes and semantic issues (valve access, maintenance clearance, penetrations through lateral elements, fire dampers, riser space, wet services over switchrooms); exports IFC4; auto-syncs issues each run.

**Business value:** Coordination problems found before drawings, not on site.

**Skills & methods**
- Parametric IFC element authoring
- AABB clash detection with typical-floor grouping
- Semantic clash rules
- IFC4 STEP export (validated with IfcOpenShell)
- Issue tracking with auto-resolution

**Inputs**
- Scheme & sized systems

**Outputs**
- IFC4 model
- Clash groups
- Issues/RFIs

**Standards:** ISO 16739 (IFC4); buildingSMART openBIM

**Collaborates with:** Construction Planning (Element-to-activity links (4D)); Cost & BOQ (Element volumes)

**Who buys it:** BIM managers, General contractors, Owners requiring openBIM deliverables

**Scope & limits:** Box geometry (LOD 200); not a replacement for authored LOD 300+ models.

## Cost & BOQ <a id="cost"></a>

**ID:** `cost` · **Discipline:** Commercial · **Plan:** Starter+

Measures quantities from the model and sized systems, builds a MasterFormat-coded BOQ with location-factored rates, and adds preliminaries, contingency, fees and escalation; reports by discipline, system and floor; CSV export.

**Business value:** A defensible cost plan the moment the scheme changes.

**Skills & methods**
- Model-based QTO
- MasterFormat BOQ
- Location factors
- Cost by discipline / floor / system
- Budget variance

**Inputs**
- Quantities
- Location
- Budget

**Outputs**
- BOQ
- Cost plan
- Cost per m²

**Standards:** CSI MasterFormat; NRM-style elemental reporting

**Collaborates with:** Value Engineering (Cost baseline); Construction Planning (Resource-loaded cost (5D))

**Who buys it:** Quantity surveyors / cost consultants, Developers, Contractors (estimating)

**Scope & limits:** Generic unit rates; calibrate with local market data.

## Value Engineering <a id="ve"></a>

**ID:** `ve` · **Discipline:** Commercial · **Plan:** Professional+

Generates alternatives (PT slabs, WWR, GGBS, concrete grade, façade type, grid, heat pumps, lift count), re-runs the full engine for each and rejects any that break drift, compliance, energy or carbon.

**Business value:** Savings that do not come back as change orders or failed inspections.

**Skills & methods**
- Alternative generation
- Full re-analysis per alternative
- Performance-consequence detection
- Cost/carbon trade-off

**Inputs**
- Baseline design & cost

**Outputs**
- Ranked VE options with consequences

**Standards:** SAVE International VE job plan (method)

**Collaborates with:** Cost & BOQ (Recommended savings)

**Who buys it:** Developers, Contractors (bid optimisation), Owner's representatives

**Scope & limits:** Explores a predefined option set.

## Construction Planning <a id="construction"></a>

**ID:** `construction` · **Discipline:** Construction · **Plan:** Professional+

Builds the activity network and CPM schedule, links model elements to activities (4D), resource-loads cost (5D S-curve), selects tower cranes for the critical lift, designs temporary works (retention, dewatering, back-propping, formwork) and flags constructability issues.

**Business value:** Programme and logistics risk visible at bid stage.

**Skills & methods**
- CPM forward/backward pass
- 4D element linking
- 5D cash flow
- Crane selection by critical lift
- Temporary-works selection & propping check
- Constructability rules

**Inputs**
- Scheme
- Foundation
- Cost plan

**Outputs**
- Gantt & critical path
- Cash flow
- Crane & logistics plan
- Temporary works
- Constructability log

**Standards:** CPM scheduling practice; BS 5975 (temporary works, reference)

**Collaborates with:** Cost & BOQ (Escalation & preliminaries timing)

**Who buys it:** General contractors, Construction managers, Developers (financing)

**Scope & limits:** Template-based activity network; not resource-levelled.

## Digital Twin & Operations <a id="operations"></a>

**ID:** `operations` · **Discipline:** Operations · **Plan:** Enterprise+

Maintains the asset register; predicts 90-day failure probability and remaining useful life (Weibull adjusted by condition and runtime); detects anomalies; recommends schedule, set-point and ventilation optimisations.

**Business value:** Fewer breakdowns and lower energy bills across the portfolio.

**Skills & methods**
- Weibull reliability & RUL
- Risk = P(fail) × criticality
- Sensor anomaly detection
- Energy vs baseline
- Optimisation recommendations

**Inputs**
- Asset register
- Sensor/BMS feeds

**Outputs**
- Asset health
- Maintenance plan
- Savings opportunities

**Standards:** ISO 55000 (asset management, reference)

**Collaborates with:** Building Physics & Energy (Measured vs design EUI)

**Who buys it:** Facility managers, REITs & portfolio owners, Hospitals & universities

**Scope & limits:** Demo uses synthetic sensor data; connect BMS/IoT feeds in production.

## Independent Verifier <a id="verifier"></a>

**ID:** `verifier` · **Discipline:** QA · **Plan:** Starter+

Checks equilibrium, Rayleigh vs eigen periods, statics vs FE, Boussinesq vs 2:1 settlement, BIM volumes vs QTO, BOQ arithmetic, energy balance and CPM closure, with tolerances and PASS/WARN/FAIL.

**Business value:** Auditable confidence in AI-assisted engineering — the key to selling to regulated buyers.

**Skills & methods**
- Global equilibrium
- Rayleigh-quotient period
- Statics cross-checks
- Alternative stress distribution
- Quantity reconciliation
- Schedule closure

**Inputs**
- All agent results

**Outputs**
- Verification report

**Standards:** Engineering QA practice

**Collaborates with:** All agents (Discrepancies for engineer review)

**Who buys it:** Engineering QA/QC leads, Checking engineers, Insurers

**Scope & limits:** Verifies consistency, not the professional judgement of a licensed engineer.
